**Finding: Deviation (medium) — MINCOMMIT**

§ 2.1 binds Customer to a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely our walk-away position. It also directly contradicts two other clauses in the same agreement:

- **§ 12.3** — Vendor "acknowledges that Customer has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment."
- **§ 7.1** — Fees are those stated in Order Forms, and Vendor "may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify."

No shortfall/true-up mechanic exists anywhere (the only "shortfall" references are in the § 22 audit provisions, which run in our favour).

**Redline (preferred, validated ok:true)** — replaces § 2.1 with: no minimum purchase, take-or-pay or volume commitment; any volume/spend figures are non-binding forecasts; payment only for Services ordered under an Order Form and, where applicable, actually used. This also removes the internal inconsistency with §§ 7.1 and 12.3. Fallback offered in the comment: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a penalty.
